metadata.description: Serialize a SHACL ShapesGraph to RDF triples using the SHACL vocabulary

literal.string: Allocate a deterministic blank node for the k-th anonymous object of a SHACL property (given by its local name) on a subject. The label is derived from the subject, the property, and the ordinal, so serialization stays pure and stable. An IRI subject is escaped to [A-Za-z0-9_] characters; a blank node subject (itself allocated here) is used as-is. Because every allocated label contains '-' and an escaped IRI never does, the labels are injective.

Escape a string for use in a blank node label: ASCII letters and digits are kept, and every other character becomes '_' followed by its decimal code point and '_'. The result is valid in N-Triples blank node labels and never contains '-'.

Serialize a list-valued SHACL property (given by its local name, e.g. sh:in) as a single triple whose object is an RDF collection: a chain of rdf:first/rdf:rest cells on deterministic blank nodes, terminated by rdf:nil. An empty list is rdf:nil itself. Cell labels use the property name suffixed with 'List', so they never collide with blank nodes allocated for the list's own members.

Serialize a reference-valued SHACL property whose value is a single SHACL list of shapes (sh:and, sh:or, sh:xone): one triple whose object is the list of referenced shapes, plus the triples of any anonymous shapes.

Resolve the k-th reference-valued object of a SHACL property (given by its local name) on a subject to an RDF node, together with any triples describing it. A named reference is its IRI; an anonymous reference is a fresh deterministic blank node, onto which the inline shape is serialized using the given function. An inline definition is its own IRI, onto which the inline shape is serialized.
